details:
Project Orion is an educational web game that places players in charge of a Dominican space mission to Mars. Through a 2D pixel-art interface, players select a crew, prepare supplies, review spacecraft systems, and guide their expedition through launch, travel, and landing.

The game includes two missions: Guandules, focused on growing pigeon peas in a Martian greenhouse, and Perseverance, centered on exploring Jezero Crater and collecting, classifying, and analyzing geological samples. Players manage oxygen, energy, food, water, and spacecraft integrity while responding to challenges that require planning and careful decisions.

The project aims to make science and technology more approachable through hands-on experimentation. Its intended benefits include encouraging curiosity about space exploration, developing resource-management and problem-solving skills, and helping players understand the connections between agriculture, engineering, health, and scientific research. These are educational goals; learning outcomes have not yet been formally evaluated.

We developed the application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Canvas for game graphics and the Web Audio API for synthesized music and sound effects. Browser storage preserves progress and preferences. ChatGPT supported code development and content drafting. The application runs in a web browser without specialized hardware. Its creative approach combines space exploration with Dominican cultural identity: a spacecraft named Quisqueya, pigeon pea cultivation, a launch setting in Pedernales, and original bachata-inspired instrumental music.

Our team considered accessibility, readability, cultural representation, and continuity of gameplay. Features include high contrast, enlarged text, reduced motion, adjustable audio, and written equivalents for sound notifications. We also distinguish simulated gameplay values from real scientific measurements and recognize the need to verify scientific references, document asset permissions, and conduct further usability testing.
